request: Review supplied candidate.py as an uncommitted new file without repair.

scope.baseline: absent file; complete supplied owned new-file bytes

spec: Admins may open every record; members may open only records from their own organization.

findings.title: Member organization predicate is inverted
findings.trigger: member org A with record org B; also member org A with record org A
findings.actual: Cross-organization record allowed; own-organization record denied.
findings.expected: Cross-organization record denied; own-organization record allowed.
findings.consequence: Members can access records outside their organization and cannot open their own records.
findings.evidence: Literal member_other_org and member_own_org cases both fail; both admin cases pass.
findings.concrete_remedy: Use an own-organization equality condition for members while retaining the admin rule. No repair performed.
findings.verification_gap: Only supplied admin/member dictionary domain is covered; unspecified roles and malformed data are outside this spec.

findings.title: Role input is routed through dynamic eval
findings.trigger: Every can_open call evaluates repr(user["role"]) with eval.
findings.actual: Dynamic evaluator consumes a representation derived from user input.
findings.expected: Use the role value without dynamic evaluation.
findings.consequence: Violates the explicit hard standard and retains an unnecessary dynamic execution surface.
findings.evidence: AST finds an eval Call at line 2; direct source inspection confirms input lineage.
findings.concrete_remedy: Remove dynamic evaluation and use validated role data directly. No repair performed.
findings.verification_gap: Arbitrary code execution from ordinary string role values was not demonstrated; repr quotes those values. Finding is the explicit standards violation.
